title: Consolidate GPU assignment protocols and refactor lease negotiator
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Reduce flakiness and high tail latencies observed during scale-up/scale-down events by consolidating multiple GPU assignment protocols and extracting a single-purpose Lease Negotiator component.

Background: Over the past year we accumulated protocol divergence between the legacy binder, leasepool reconciler, and the newer fast-assign path. This has manifested as transient double-allocations, long reconciliation loops, and two classes of race conditions during preemption and graceful drain. Recent incidents (incident-2025-11-gpu-hotloop) investigated in the ops runbook point to unclear handoffs between ‘claim’ and ‘hold’ states.

Goals:
- Extract a Lease Negotiator service that ownly (sic) handles lease offers, confirmations, and revocations with idempotent receipts.
- Replace ad-hoc assignment state machine with a single canonical assignment protocol (v2) while keeping backwards-compatibility during rollout.
- Add comprehensive metrics and tracing: per-lease lifecycle histograms, binding retry counts, and end-to-end assignment latency.
- Reduce p95 assignment latency by 30% and eliminate double-allocations in normal churn.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Backwards compatible adapter: existing node agents will continue to understand the legacy binder messages. We will introduce assignment_v2 feature flag in runtime config to gate behavior. This gives safer rollouts but increases code paths temporarily.
- Event-sourced vs in-memory FSM: chose lightweight event-sourcing for the Negotiator (durable append-only log backed by existing rabbit queue) to make post-mortem reconstructions possible. The trade-off is slightly higher write amplification; mitigated via batching.
- Lease receipt idempotency requires adding a 128-bit receipt id to all lease packets and storing recent receipts in a bounded LRU on the node agent. This increases memory footprint per agent but prevents duplicate activations.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prototype Negotiator service and wire a read-only adapter into the allocator (experimental feature flag).
2) Implement assignment_v2 protocol and add schema versioning to assignment messages.
3) Run end-to-end tests in staging with synthetic churn workload (workloads/churn-generator) and measure assignment latencies and duplicate allocation rate.
4) Canary deploy in us-west-2 dedicated pool at 5% traffic, monitor for 48h, then 25%, then full rollout.

Observability and alerts:
- New dashboards: /dashboards/gpu/assignment-lifecycle (Grafana) and a high-cardinality trace span 'negotiator.assign' in X-Ray.
- Alerts: p95 assignment latency > 750ms for 5m, duplicate-allocation-rate > 0.1% for 15m.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- During rollout, the Negotiator will accept legacy binding tokens and emit adapter events. Nodes still on the old agent will function; only the allocator moves to the Negotiator first.
- Migration job: a background job will mark leases with negotiated=true once observed stable for N cycles; this avoids churn spikes.

Security and compliance considerations:
- Lease receipts are not sensitive but we will sign receipts with the node’s ephemeral key to avoid tampering. No PII is involved.
- security_review_required: false (low risk), but cryptographic signing will be reviewed by security FYI.

Rollback plan:
- Feature flag toggle to revert allocator to legacy binder. If duplicate allocations increase post-rollout, revert to 5% and investigate. Full rollback if SLA breaches.

Deliverables:
- Negotiator service (go) + adapter library for allocator and node-agent (go/rust).
- New integration tests and a synthetic churn harness.
- Dashboards and alerts.
- Runbook entry and postmortem template for any regression.

comments: 2026-02-11 - Asha Patel: Created ticket; initial design sketch attached. Noted that recent churn tests show duplicate allocations ~0.6% under 1000-node churn. Asked infra to reserve a small staging pool.

2026-02-20 - Miguel Ortega: Prototype Negotiator service skeleton pushed in feature branch. Basic API: OfferLease(leaseId, nodeId), Confirm(leaseId, receipt), Revoke(leaseId). Added initial receipts implementation (PR #8472).

2026-02-28 - Code review (Sana Li): Requested clearer invariants around Confirm idempotency and stricter test coverage for split-brain scenarios. Miguel to add end-to-end test that simulates kv-store partition.
2026-03-03 - Miguel Ortega: Added batched write path to reduce write amplification; local benchmark shows 12% CPU overhead at peak vs 30% for naive writes.

2026-03-08 - QA (Jordan Kim): Staging churn harness results: p95 assignment latency down from 980ms to 640ms for v2, duplicate allocations eliminated in 10/10 runs. Noted a sporadic 502 from adapter under heavy partitioning - follow-up created.
2026-03-12 - Release lead (Priya Nair): Approved canary plan for us-west-2 (5% -> 25% -> 100%) pending one more fix for adapter 502; target canary start 2026-03-18.
